title: Replace deprecated `with_mock()` with `with_mocked_bindings()`
description:
Migrates test mocking from deprecated `with_mock()` to `with_mocked_bindings()` for testthat v3.3.0+ compatibility.

### Changes
- Replaced three `with_mock()` calls in `tests/testthat/test-keyboard.R`
- Used `with_mocked_bindings()` to maintain original scoping behavior
- Expectations remain wrapped inside the mocking calls for proper scope isolation
- Removed `.env` parameter (not used by `with_mocked_bindings()`)

### Before/After
```r
# Before
with_mock(
  write_addins = function(...) TRUE,
  is_interactive = function(...) TRUE,
  .env = "shrtcts",
  expect_message(add_rstudio_shortcuts(tmp_shrtcts, tmp_addins))
)

# After
with_mocked_bindings(
  write_addins = function(...) TRUE,
  is_interactive = function(...) TRUE,
  {
    expect_message(add_rstudio_shortcuts(tmp_shrtcts, tmp_addins))
  }
)
```

`with_mocked_bindings()` wraps code in a block where mocks are active, matching the original `with_mock()` behavior where each mock was scoped to a single expectation. The `.package` argument is not needed when mocking functions in the package under test.

# Temporarily redefine function definitions

Source: [`R/mock2.R`](https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/blob/v3.3.1/R/mock2.R)

`local_mocked_bindings.Rd`

`with_mocked_bindings()` and `local_mocked_bindings()` provide tools for "mocking", temporarily redefining a function so that it behaves differently during tests. This is helpful for testing functions that depend on external state (i.e. reading a value from a file or a website, or pretending a package is or isn't installed).

Learn more in `[vignette("mocking")](https://testthat.r-lib.org/articles/mocking.html)`.

## Usage[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#ref-usage)

```
local_mocked_bindings(..., .package = NULL, .env = caller_env())

with_mocked_bindings(code, ..., .package = NULL)
```

## Arguments[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#arguments)

...[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#arg--)

Name-value pairs providing new values (typically functions) to temporarily replace the named bindings.

.package[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#arg--package)

The name of the package where mocked functions should be inserted. Generally, you should not supply this as it will be automatically detected when whole package tests are run or when there's one package under active development (i.e. loaded with `[pkgload::load_all()](https://pkgload.r-lib.org/reference/load_all.html)`). We don't recommend using this to mock functions in other packages, as you should not modify namespaces that you don't own.

.env[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#arg--env)

Environment that defines effect scope. For expert use only.

code[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#arg-code)

Code to execute with specified bindings.

## Use[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#use)

There are four places that the function you are trying to mock might come from:

- Internal to your package.
    
- Imported from an external package via the `NAMESPACE`.
    
- The base environment.
    
- Called from an external package with `::`.
    

They are described in turn below.

(To mock S3 & S4 methods and R6 classes see `[local_mocked_s3_method()](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_s3_method.html)`, `[local_mocked_s4_method()](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_s3_method.html)`, and `[local_mocked_r6_class()](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_r6_class.html)`.)

### Internal & imported functions[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#internal-amp-imported-functions)

You mock internal and imported functions the same way. For example, take this code:

```
some_function <- function() {
  another_function()
}
```

It doesn't matter whether `another_function()` is defined by your package or you've imported it from a dependency with `@import` or `@importFrom`, you mock it the same way:

```
local_mocked_bindings(
  another_function = function(...) "new_value"
)
```

### Base functions[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#base-functions)

To mock a function in the base package, you need to make sure that you have a binding for this function in your package. It's easiest to do this by binding the value to `NULL`. For example, if you wanted to mock `[interactive()](https://rdrr.io/r/base/interactive.html)` in your package, you'd need to include this code somewhere in your package:

```
interactive <- NULL
```

Why is this necessary? `with_mocked_bindings()` and `local_mocked_bindings()` work by temporarily modifying the bindings within your package's namespace. When these tests are running inside of `R CMD check` the namespace is locked which means it's not possible to create new bindings so you need to make sure that the binding exists already.

### Namespaced calls[](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/local_mocked_bindings.html#namespaced-calls)

It's trickier to mock functions in other packages that you call with `::`. For example, take this minor variation:

```
some_function <- function() {
  anotherpackage::another_function()
}
```

To mock this function, you'd need to modify `another_function()` inside the `anotherpackage` package. You _can_ do this by supplying the `.package` argument to `local_mocked_bindings()` but we don't recommend it because it will affect all calls to `anotherpackage::another_function()`, not just the calls originating in your package. Instead, it's safer to either import the function into your package, or make a wrapper that you can mock:

  my_wrapper()
}

title: feat: Add `shortcut_run()` and `shortcut_get()`
description:
Makes it easier to get and run shortcuts by name (assigned name in the R code sense) when using `.shrtcts.R`.

This in turn makes it possible to use shrtcts to store workflow shortcuts and to run these shortcuts in Positron.

title: Change documentation to improve performance for scripts
description:
The instructions for loading the package in `.Rprofile` are currently given as

> ```r
> if (interactive() & requireNamespace("shrtcts", quietly = TRUE)) {
>   shrtcts::add_rstudio_shortcuts()
> }
> ```

This has the effect of *always* executing `requireNamespace`, even when not in interactive mode. By using short-circuited `&&` instead of `&`, this PR improves the performance of running non-interactive scripts by never attempting to load the package.

title: Use .shrtcts.R + roxygen2 and add keybinding management
description:
:partying_face: Two features for the price of one PR!

## Introducing `.shrtcts.R`

This PR officially switches **shrtcts** from using painful YAML files like this

```yaml
- name: Restart RStudio
  id: 5
  shortcut: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+R
  Interactive: true
  Binding: usethis:::restart_rstudio
```

to plain R scripts annotated with roxyen2 tags:

```r
#' Restart RStudio
#'
#' @id 5
#' @shortcut Ctrl+Alt+Shift+R
#' @interactive
usethis:::restart_rstudio
```

(Okay, this example isn't too painful in YAML, but multi-line shortcuts in YAML blocks were definitely not fun.)

YAML files are still supported, but the `.shrtcts.R` file gets preferential treatment and I've shifted the focus of documentation to the new R script format.

I've included an internal function that rewrites `.shrtcts.yml` to `.shrtcts.R`

```r
# migrate current .shrtcts.yml
shrtcts:::migrate_yaml2r()

# migrate specific .shrtcts.yml
shrtcts:::migrate_yaml2r("path/to/.shrtcts.yml")

# preview output (or specify output path)
shrtcts:::migrate_yaml2r(output = NULL)
```

Check that your shortcuts still work as expected (who knows, I ~~may have~~ probably missed an edge case) and then delete the old `.shrtcts.yml`.

## Automatic keybinding management

Also included in this PR is a new feature to automatically manage shortcut keybindings, thanks to @pat-s for the nudge in #6. 

To make this work, assign keybindings to shortcuts with a `@shortcut` tag (use RStudio menu for style guide), e.g. `#' @shortcut Ctrl+Cmd+Shift+L`.

Then call `add_rstudio_shortcuts(set_keyboard_shortcuts = TRUE)` or add the argument to `add_rstudio_shortcuts()` in your `~/.Rprofile`. Either way, a full restart of RStudio is required after shrtcts updates the keybindings and it creates a backup (`addins.json.bak`) prior to writing. Only shrtcts-related shortcuts are managed. More details in the README and `?add_rstudio_shortcuts`.
